Hence, the correct answer is **"156".**

questions.question:
By interchanging which two signs and two numbers (not digits) the equation will be correct?

5 - 7 × 4 + 8 ÷ 2 = 17
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f1f11fbb4e091305a6b414e74c3aec25b8d519670a1f3bd65f5bd4eb1bdcd68.png] 

Given equation: 5 - 7 × 4 + 8 ÷ 2 = 17

Option 1) - and ÷, 5 and 4

By interchanging which two signs and two numbers (not digits):

⇒ __**4 ÷ 7 × 5**__ + 8 - 2 = 17

⇒ __2.85__ + 8 - 2 = 17

⇒ __10.8____**5**____** - 2**__ = 17

⇒ 8.85 = 17

Option 2) + and -, 2 and 5

By interchanging which two signs and two numbers (not digits):

⇒ 2 + 7 × 4 - __**8 ÷ 5**__ = 17

⇒ 2 + __**7 × 4**__ - 1.6 = 17

⇒ __**2 + 28**__ - 1.6 = 17

⇒ __30____** - 1.6**__ = 17

⇒ 28.4 = 17

Option 3) ÷ and -, 7 and 8 

By interchanging which two signs and two numbers (not digits):

⇒ __**5 ÷ 8 × 4**__ + 7 - 2 = 17

⇒ **__2.5__**__** + 7 - 2**__ = 17

⇒ __**9.5 - 2**__ = 17

⇒ 7.5 = 17

**Option 4) × and +, 4 and 5**

By interchanging which two signs and two numbers (not digits):

⇒ 4 - 7 + 5 × __**8 ÷ 2**__ = 17

⇒ 4 - 7 + __**5 **____**× **____4__ = 17

⇒ __**4**__ - 7 + **__20__** = 17

⇒ __**24 - 7**__ = 17

⇒** 17** = 17

Hence, the correct answer is** "× and +, 4 and 5".**

questions.question: Which dancing form is classified as Ekaharya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam is the Indian classical dance form that is classified as Ekaharya**
 
• Ekaharya is a** technique in Bharatnatyam where a single dancer plays multiple roles in a single performance. **
 
• **Other features**
 
 
• Bharatnatyam is a popular dance form in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
 
• It is known for its storytelling, footwork, hand movements, facial expressions, and acrobatic dancing. 
 
• The Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur has been a center for Bharatnatyam since 1000 CE.
 
• The Tanjore Quartette is said to have been responsible for the current repertoire of Bharatnatyam in the early 19th century. 
 
• The Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikesvara is a primary text used to study the technique and grammar of body movement in Bharatnatyam
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odissi, Sattriya, and Kathak are all classical dances of India: 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• This dance originated in Odisha, India's easternmost state.
 
• It is primarily a dance for women, with postures that are similar to those found in temple sculptures. 
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**
 
 
• This dance is from Assam and is associated with the Sattras (Vaishnava maths or monasteries).
 
• It is governed by strict principles for footwork, hastamudras, aharyas, and music. 
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• This dance originated in Uttar Pradesh (U.P) in North India.
 
• The word Kathak means story, and dancers narrate stories through their expressions and eyes.

questions.question: In the context of the Indian census, what is the definition of the literacy percentage?

options.text: The percentage of people aged seven and above, who can read and write in any language
The percentage of people with a college degree
The percentage of people who can read and write in English
The percentage of people who can perform basic arithmetic calculations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the Indian census, *l**iteracy rate***** is a measure of the proportion of people in a population who have basic reading and writing skills in any language.**
 
• This definition does not require fluency or advanced literacy skills but simply the ability to read and write with comprehension.
 
• T**he literacy rate considers individuals aged seven years and above.**
 
• This age threshold is set because, by this age, most children have started schooling and are expected to acquire basic reading and writing skills
 
• Literacy does not imply having a college degree or advanced education
 
• **It simply means the ability to read and write with understanding.**
 
• The l**iteracy rate counts people who can read and write in any language, not necessarily English or Hindi.**
 
• This inclusivity is important in a multilingual country like India.

• **Ghaffar Khan was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi** and a prominent advocate of non-violence.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The founder of the Mauryan dynasty, Chandragupta united the Indian subcontinent in the 4th century BC.
 
• After his political and military unification, he sought out monasticism and lived as a Jain.
 
• His court advisor and Kautilya was also known for his cunning statecraft and expansionary mindset.
 
• The two of them created an empire rarely rivaled in Indian history.

 
• The capital of Chandragupta's empire was Pataliputra near the Ganges river in northeastern India.
 
 
• A description of the city in the time of Chandragupta comes from the Greek traveler Megasthenes.
 
• It was known for being one of the largest cities in the world at the time of the Mauryan empire.
 
• The shape of the city was a parallelogram and apparently had 64 gates in its wooden walls.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• He was also known as Devanam Priyadasi.
 
• Ashoka invaded Kalinga in 261 B.C., in what is famously known as the Kalinga War.
 
• After witnessing the massive loss of life and suffering during the Kalinga War, he decided to end military conquests and converted to Buddhism.
 
• Ashoka promoted the spread of Buddhism across ancient Asia, becoming a significant patron of the religion.
 
• He was the first king in Indian history to document his achievements and messages on stones, known as Rock Edicts.
 
• The Great Stupa at Sanchi was built during Ashoka’s reign to commemorate the spread of Buddhism.

 
• Major Rock Edict 13 provides detailed information about his Kalinga War.
 
• There are a total of fourteen Major Rock Edicts.
 
• The two Kalinga Edicts are located in the newly conquered Kalinga territory.
 
• Major Pillar Edicts were erected in important cities to spread Ashoka’s messages.
 
• In addition to Major Rock Edicts, there are Minor Rock Edicts and Minor Pillar Edicts.
 
• Kalinga War
 
 
• Ashoka, the son of the Mauryan emperor Bindusara and grandson of Chandragupta Maurya, ascended the throne of Magadha in 273 B.C.
 
• Following the expansionist tradition of his ancestors, Ashoka sought to expand his empire further.
 
• In the 12th year of his reign, he sent a message to Kalinga (present-day Odisha) asking for its submission to the Mauryan empire. The Kalingaraj, however, refused to surrender.
 
• The Kalinga War was fought on the Dhauli hills along the banks of the Daya River.
 
• In 261 B.C., Ashoka led a vast army against Kalinga.
 
• The fiercely independent people of Kalinga mounted a strong defense against the Mauryan forces.
 
• Despite their determination and courage, the limited forces of Kalinga were no match for the massive Magadha army.
 
• The people of Kalinga displayed remarkable valor, nearly securing victory on several occasions.
 
• Ultimately, Ashoka's forces prevailed, but at an enormous cost to life and property. The entire region of Kalinga was left devastated.
 
• Ashoka’s 13th Rock Edict vividly describes the horrors and bloodshed of the Kalinga War.
 
• In about 263 B.C., after reflecting on the war’s destruction, Ashoka embraced Buddhism under the guidance of the monk Moggaliputta Tissa, who became his mentor.

Marked Price (MP) = Selling Price / (1 - Discount Rate)

**Calculation:**

Discount Rate = 33% = 33 / 100 = 0.33

MP = SP / (1 - Discount Rate)
